_conversion_info.note: Genesys and SWRPG share the same narrative dice symbol system, so this is a 1:1 shorthand swap, not a rules conversion. No talent required judgement-call symbol changes.
_conversion_info.force_field: Every talent now carries "force": "Yes"/"No". Force talents (Yes) can only be bought by Force Sensitive characters (see force_rules).

talents.name: Animal Companion
talents.text_original_genesys: Your character creates a bond with a single animal approved by your GM. This animal must be silhouette 0 (no larger than a mid-sized dog). The bond persists as long as your character chooses, although at your GM’s discretion, the bond may also be broken due to abusive treatment or other extenuating circumstances. As long as the bond persists, the animal follows your character, and you dictate the animal’s overall behavior (although, since the animal is only bonded with the character, not dominated, it may still perform inconvenient actions such as scratching furniture, consuming rations, and marking territory). Once per round in structured encounters, your character may spend one maneuver to direct their animal in performing one action and one maneuver during your character’s turn. The animal must be within hearing and visual range of your character (generally medium range) to do this. Otherwise, the animal does not contribute to the encounter. The specifics of its behavior are up to you and your GM. For every additional rank of Animal Companion your character has, increase the allowed silhouette of the companion by one (this may mean your character gets a new companion, or their companion grows in size). This talent can also change in flavor depending on the nature of your game setting. While an animal companion may make sense in many settings, in a futuristic setting it may make more sense for the “animal” to be a robot or drone, for example.

force_rules.Force Sensitive: Only characters that are Force Sensitive are able to feel or access The Force. A character must be Force Sensitive to purchase any Force talents (labeled with Force: Yes). There are two ways for a PC to become Force Sensitive: species special ability or the Force Sensitive talent.
force_rules.Committing Force Dice: Some Force talents may reference "committing" a Force die. A committed die comes from your character's pool of ⚪ provided by their Force rating and cannot be used to activate other Force talents while it is committed. Any effects being maintained by a committed die can be ended at the end of any character's turn as an incidental.
force_rules.Combined Checks: Some Force talents have your character make a skill check in addition to activating the talent with ⚪. When a ⚪ is rolled with a skill check ◑ may be spent to add ✔ or ▲, player's choice.
force_rules.Resisting Force Powers: Any character being targeted by a Force talent may resist the effects if they wish. If they choose to resist an effect and the talent does not already use a check, the user of the Force talent must make an opposed Discipline vs Discipline check. Additionally, the target may roll ⚪ up to their Force Rating. ◑ may be spent to add ✖ or ▼ to the check.
force_rules.Range: If the description of a Force talent refers to the range in which it is effective, that range can be extended. ◑ may be spent to increase the range of any Force talent by one. This effect may be activated a number of times up to your character's Force Rating. This option is always available and is not an additional XP expenditure.
force_rules.Duration: If the description of a Force talent refers to the duration or time span in which it is effective, that duration can be extended. ◑ may be spent to increase the number of rounds or minutes of any Force talent is active by one. This effect may be activated a number of times up to your character's Force Rating. This option is always available and is not an additional XP expenditure.
force_rules.Magnitude: If the description of a Force talent refers to targets on which is applies an effect, that number of targets can be extended. ◑ may be spent to increase the number of targets of any Force talent by one. This effect may be activated a number of times up to your character's Force Rating. This option is always available and is not an additional XP expenditure.
force_rules.Morality: Use Morality from the F&D book as-is for now. Optional Rule: Each time a character receives Conflict roll 1d10, rather than at the end of each session. If the value on the die is above the amount of Conflict the PC currently has, nothing happens. If below, the PC's Morality is reduced by the value on the die and the PC's Conflict is set to 0. Conflict points may only be removed if the character performs actions that make positive use of their Emotional Strength or face-off and resist their Emotional Weakness. If at the end of a session or major story beat (GM choice) the PC has 0 Conflict, they roll 1d5. The PC increases their Morality score by that amount.
